analyzed_vuln.description: In SipRequestFirstLine::SipRequestFirstLine(SipRequestLayer*), parseVersion() can set m_VersionOffset to -1 when a SIP version token is not found in malformed input. The constructor then unconditionally does memchr(m_Data + m_VersionOffset, '\n', m_DataLen - (size_t)m_VersionOffset). Because m_VersionOffset is negative, pointer arithmetic goes out of bounds and the computed length underflows to a huge size, causing an invalid read/SEGV inside memchr.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: FuzzTarget parses packet bytes into UDP, and UdpLayer::parseNextLayer() classifies payload as SIP request if parseMethod() recognizes a method token. A crafted UDP payload on SIP ports that has a valid-looking SIP method but lacks/invalidates the expected version pattern (' SIP/') makes parseVersion() fail (m_VersionOffset=-1). Constructor still calls memchr with that invalid offset, triggering OOB read and crash.
